items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the New York state urban development corporation act and the
economic development law, in relation to the creation of micro-business worker
cooperatives upon transfer of ownership

items.lawSection: New York State Urban Development Corporation Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2176

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the New York state urban development corporation act and
the economic development law, in relation to the creation of micro-busi-
ness worker cooperatives upon transfer of ownership

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would provide for assistance in the creation of micro-business
worker cooperatives upon transfer of ownership of an existing business.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would add a new paragraph (o) to subdivision 1 of section 16-m
of the New York State Urban Development Corporation Act that would make
micro-business worker cooperatives upon transfer of ownership of an
existing business, eligible to apply for assistance under the Economic
Development Fund.

Further, this legislation would amend section 104-a of the Economic
Development Law relating to Department of Economic Development to
provide assistance to micro-business worker cooperatives by expanding
the State entities that the Department must work in cooperation with the
Empire State Development Corporation and any other applicable state
agency or office.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The purpose of this legislation is to provide an additional source of
funding to eligible worker-owned cooperatives upon the transfer of
ownership of an existing micro-business. This legislation would help
ensure that a viable business remains open and that the workers current-
ly employed by a business would have the ability to buy an existing
business. Creation of worker cooperatives is another tool to help
support a vibrant Main Street in our communities.

Historically, worker cooperatives offer workers with the opportunity to
become business owners. Worker ownership would convey to the workers the
opportunity to further improve their business, have increased control
over their work environment, and increased their long-term job security.
Worker cooperative also provide economic benefits to their home communi-
ties in the form of a stable tax base and retention of valuable jobs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2015-16: A.10099 (Thiele)- Passed Assembly
2017-18: Tabled

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided, however, that the
amendments to section sixteen-m of the Urban Development Corporation Act
made by section one of this act shall not affect the expiration of such
section and shall be deemed to expire therewith.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 65
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2176, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend the New York state urban development corporation
      act and the economic development law, in relation to the  creation
      of micro-business worker cooperatives upon transfer of ownership"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill would provide for assistance in the creation of micro-busi-
ness worker cooperatives upon transfer of ownership of an existing busi-
ness.
 
  In order to identify  additional  programs  specifically  targeted  to
assist  employee-owned enterprises, the Advisory Panel on Employee-Owned
Enterprises was created by statute in 2018. (C.30, L. 2018).  The  advi-
sory  panel  is  tasked  with  issuing a report on the state of employee
owned enterprises, which would necessarily include micro-business worker
cooperatives, and providing comprehensive recommendations.  The  2020-21
budget extended the deadline for the panel's report to 2021. It would be
premature to enact this legislation prior to being afforded the opportu-
nity to consider the panel's work and recommendations.
 
  The  State  has  already  appropriated  funds for established programs
tailored to provide financial and technical assistance  to  small  busi-
nesses.  For  example,  the  Entrepreneurial  Assistance  Centers  (EAC)
provide instruction, training and technical assistance to new  entrepre-
neurs  through  24  Centers across the state, specifically in distressed
neighborhoods, and to microenterprises and low-income  individuals.  EAC
also provides business counseling on business ownership, including coop-
erative  formation. More than 75% percent of EAC clients are microenter-
prises. Additionally, the Alternative Lenders Program  provides  support
to  alternative  lenders  from  community  development  financial insti-
tutions, community banks, credit unions, and nonprofit organizations  to
meet  the  financing needs of microenterprises; Business Mentor NY helps
microenterprises grow through access to free business mentors;  and  the
Linked  Deposit Program helps existing firms obtain reduced-rate financ-
ing so they can undertake investments to make borrowing less expensive.
 
  I remain fully committed to strategies and programs geared to  support
small  businesses,  which  are  at  the heart of re-building the State's
economy. This bill, while well intended, suffers from the same fundamen-
tal flaws as the identical bill I was  constrained  to  veto  previously
(Veto  274  of 2018), in that it would create a new grant program funded
through the Economic Development Fund, which  is  fully  committed,  and
thus  would  necessarily reduce funding for established programs. I have
vetoed similar bills in the past which sought to create  grant  programs
funded  through the Economic Development Fund as those bills should have
been considered in the context of the budget. For the foregoing reasons,
I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
